column7: Read-first note: claims here mix Apple docs with community measurement — check the attribution before acting
compile exits 0 for any arch; codes track device ids, not names — green CI, invalidCompiledModel in users' hands
A successful load is not a fit test — first inference adds activations and KV, and compute unit moves headroom 2×
The individual symbol pages disagree with the framework page — Apple docs conflict on this behavior
AOT compilation has a far narrower hardware floor than the framework — AOT assets exclude devices the framework supports
TOC: coreai-build compile succeeds for architectures the device will reject — only a device load validates
TOC: bookmarks quietly die — init?(resolvingBookmark:) returns nil, not an error, once the entry is purged
TOC: two slightly different options structs silently create two multi-gigabyte specializations
Do not copy the quoted Background Assets keys into a 27 project — one developer's 26-era config for a removed feature
Architecture codes track device identifiers, not marketing names — 'iPhone 17 Pro' reads h17p but is h18p
A green compile the device rejects — exit 0 proves nothing; the failure is invalidCompiledModel in the field
xcrun coreai-build compile exits 0 for architectures the device will reject — only a device load validates
expectFrequentReshapes=true on a fixed-shape graph abandons the AOT specialization — device-validated, can SIGSEGV
Prewarming a graph with static-shape host KV I/O allocates the whole cache up front — a net loss; gate your prewarm
Specialization reports no progress — minutes of silence that read as a hang
The specialization gauge appears only when you directly link CoreAI.framework — transitive linkage shows nothing
Apple's docs contradict each other on deleting a cache entry a live AIModel still references
Reference pages say deleting an in-use entry throws; Apple's other doc says deferred — code for both outcomes
A stored bookmark quietly stops working — purge or invalidation makes resolve return nil, not an error
bookmarkData doesn't pin the entry; resolvingBookmark returns nil, not an error — failure lands in an else branch
Code comment marks the silent branch: a well-formed bookmark whose entry is gone resolves to nil
Bookmark cleanup hits the same doc contradiction as §7.4 — in-use deletion is documented both ways
SpecializationOptions is part of the cache key — two variants mean two multi-gigabyte specializations
Slightly different SpecializationOptions from two code paths silently double the multi-GB cache and re-stall first load
Code comment: set expectFrequentReshapes explicitly false on static graphs — asking was measured to kill AOT and SIGSEGV
Code comment: match path components exactly — contains('ane') also matches 'gated-deltanet'
The app-group cache init returns nil and Apple's sample answers with fatalError — copy it and config errors crash
A bad app-group entitlement silently drops to the per-bundle cache — specialization cost and storage double
Extension memory limits count Core AI models — a model fine in the app can jetsam its extension
Every OS update purges all specialized assets regardless of cache policy — they are OS-version specific
.persistent turns off source-deletion reclamation — deleted sources strand multi-GB orphans until the next OS update
Code comment: the storage figure counts source assets only — specialized copies in the cache are invisible to it
Status note: thread 836810 is answered by Apple staff — what's missing is the capability, not the answer
iOS 27 betas report appleIntelligenceNotEnabled unless Siri is on — Apple-confirmed bug; don't require Siri in UX
Guided generation (@Generable) is not supported on GPU-pipelined engines
Grammar-constrained decoding needs logits; GPU-pipelined bundles never expose them — fastest backend loses @Generable
TOC: load OK, run dead — a model that loads can still die on its first inference step
Loading establishes weights only; the first step adds activations, workspace, maybe a full-context KV cache
iPad RAM follows storage tier — 1–2 TB iPad Pros have more RAM; same-name smaller models jetsam your tested config
mmap'd weights look free until touched — residency grows to full size on unified memory; headroom checks lie
Measured ceiling: an 18 GB int4 35B gets signal 9 on a 12 GB iPhone 17 Pro — ~5–6 GB is the phone-class limit
The same 1.8 GB core leaves ~2.8 GB headroom via ANE but ~6.0 GB via GPU — no API reports the difference
The GPU cache-limit API has two spellings across versions — check which one your installed version has
Forum 824753 (community, status unknown): ~40 GiB of 'other' allocations — watch for runaway growth
Memory-pressure trim freed an in-flight MTLBuffer (mlx#3689) — surfaces as a GPU InvalidResource error, hiding the cause
There is no NPU priority entitlement or API — Apple staff confirmed on thread 833666
Read the attribution first: community-measured on beta OSes — protocol, not gospel
Your build machine is a benchmark variable — the same export can be 2.2× slower and 2× heavier with zero diagnostics
Foundation Models exposes no tokenizer — every published tok/s figure for Apple's model is an estimate
Third-party tok/s for Apple's model carries ~±20% error — no tokenizer to count with, and nothing marks the estimates
